newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity ends mostly up with firmer cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity ends mostly up with firmer cash.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures settled mostly higher Thursday in narrow trading amid firming spot cash power prices in the western U.S.
Firm, peak electricity for Friday at Palo Verde (PV) and California-Oregon Border (COB) rose 50 cents a megawatt hour (MWh) from Thursday's level.
The cash market today took cue from the Bonneville Power Administration, which withdrew surplus offers for Friday due to higher heating demand in the West, brokers and traders said.
Strengthening values in spring and summer quarterly business bolstered the front-month contracts, they said.
March California-Oregon Border (COB) finished up 23 cents at $11.03 a megawatt hour (MWh) after bouncing between $10.90 and $11.10.
April COB ended up 10 cents at $10.10. Other active COB contracts settled five to 20 cents higher.
March Palo Verde (PV) futures ended up 18 cents at $13.28 after traded in a 30 cent range.
April PV settled down 10 cents at $12.10. Other active PV months finished five to 20 cents higher.
Forecasts showed the Pacific Northwest will experience colder temperatures into next week, with readings averaging two to eight degrees Fahrenheit below normal.

The Southwest is expected to receive frigid weather over the next several days with readings averaging eight to 12 degrees below normal. Temperatures were then expected to return to normal levels next week.
March Henry Hub natural gas futures settled down 6.9 cents at $2.361 per million British thermal units.
Swing gas deliveries at the San Juan Hub in New Mexico were assessed near $2.30/mmBtu, down about five cents from Wednesday's level.

Separately, 350 megawatt (MW) unit 2 at the San Juan coal-fired generation station was heard shut Wednesday for unspecified problems. Its operating status could not be confirmed as of Thursday morning.
A 1,100 megawatt (MW) pumped storage hydroelectric plant near Fresno, Calif., was shut last Saturday for mechanical repairs, and could stay down for up to two weeks.
The 1,158 MW WNP-2 nuclear power plant at Richland, Wash., will reduce power to 25 pct of capacity through Friday due to ongoing problems with an adjustble speed drive.
NYMEX estimated 392 COB and 168 PV futures contracts were sold, down from Wednesday's sales of 415 COB and 599 PV.
